supporting_observations.claim: The available records show repeated HTTPS CONNECT attempts from WS-NKIM-01 to update.casebinder.co at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:42:26 through 14:06:33; the proxy returned status 200 for these attempts.

Network events are attributed to process 4432, C:\Users\noah.kim\AppData\Local\CaseBinder\casebinderupd.exe, which ran as noah.kim; this differs from the inventory-listed approved updater path under C:\Program Files\CaseBinder\.
The CaseBinder-named executable was recorded as creating a file at its own path shortly after it started; the records do not establish why this occurred.

The hostname contacted is the inventory-approved CaseBinder update domain, and the observed cadence is consistent with the inventory-described update check interval; these facts support a possible benign explanation but do not resolve the executable-path discrepancy.
At 14:12:02, a further attempt to reach update.casebinder.co received proxy status 407 (authentication required), after which the CaseBinder process was recorded as exiting.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT metadata and byte counts, but the provided records do not expose the HTTPS application payload or what, if anything, the updater downloaded.
The provided records do not establish the executable's hash, signature, provenance, or whether it was an authorized per-user installation.
The records establish network activity for the listed times but do not provide enough context to determine what caused the file creation at the executable's path (T165-00118, T165-00120).
claims_not_established: Whether the AppData executable is a legitimate CaseBinder updater or an impersonating or modified binary.
Whether any update or other content was downloaded, installed, or executed as a result of these connections.
Whether the activity was initiated or authorized by Noah Kim or by an administrator.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the executable and verify its hash, digital signature, file metadata, and provenance against a trusted CaseBinder distribution.
Review endpoint or proxy TLS-inspection and download records, if available, for the content and update response associated with these connections.
Check CaseBinder installation and update records, including whether a per-user installation or update was authorized at this time.
Preserve and examine relevant endpoint artifacts, including the file creation and process history around 13:41:59–13:42:03 UTC.
unrelated_findings: Chrome was launched to Google Drive and the proxy recorded access to drive.google.com; Google Drive is not among the approved services listed in the environment context. This is separate from the alerted CaseBinder connections (T165-00019, T165-00024, T165-00025).

GlobalProtect and Cisco AnyConnect client processes were observed on WS-NKIM-01, although the environment context says there is no VPN. The records establish process execution, not an active VPN connection (T165-00016, T165-00018, T165-00221, T165-00222).
FILE-MAP-01 made a connection attempt to WS-NKIM-01 on port 3389 that ended in S0 with no bytes recorded; this is outside the alerted outbound HTTPS activity (T165-00010, T165-00012).

DC-MAP-01 made connection attempts to WS-NKIM-01 on ports 443 and 22; the records show a rejected connection on port 443 and an S0 connection on port 22. These are separate inbound attempts, not the alerted outbound HTTPS activity (T165-00177, T165-00178, T165-00179, T165-00180).
